author: Grand Canyon Times
title: Cochise County Board adopts updated building codes, effective September 1
text:
Cochise County Board adopts updated building codes, effective September 1
The Cochise County Board of Supervisors voted on July 15 to adopt Resolution 26-23, updating the county’s building and safety codes for construction in areas under county jurisdiction. The updated standards will take effect September 1.
The board’s action replaces most of the currently adopted 2015 international codes with the 2024 editions and updates the National Electrical Code from the 2014 to the 2023 edition. It also adopts the 2024 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code while continuing use of the 2012 International Energy Conservation Code.
Development Services Director Christine McLachlan said, “The goal was to modernize the County’s core construction standards without losing the practical flexibility that matters in a rural county. These locally amended codes provide builders and property owners with clearer, more consistent standards while continuing to recognize owner-builders, alternative construction methods and conditions specific to Cochise County.”
Local amendments include expanded permit exemptions for common residential improvements, longer commercial permit and application timelines, and design criteria addressing local wind, snow, floodplain and climatic conditions. The amendments also continue support for alternative construction methods such as straw bale and rammed-earth when approved by the County Building Official. Permit exemptions now apply to certain detached accessory structures up to 200 square feet, qualifying window and door replacements, reroofing without structural changes, gutters and downspouts installation, insulation work, some like-for-like plumbing repairs, as well as adoption of an appendix covering tiny houses.
The decision followed months of technical review and public engagement through meetings with advisory boards, stakeholder outreach efforts including a builders’ roundtable session, a board work session and public hearings before both Planning & Zoning Commission members as well as supervisors themselves. Permit applications submitted before September 1 will be reviewed under current codes; those submitted on or after that date will follow new requirements. Development Services staff plan updates to forms and guidance documents, along with outreach ahead of implementation.
In other aspects of Cochise County education performance during recent years: in grades three through eight during the 2022-23 school year AASA exam cycle only about one-third passed English or mathematics sections; similarly low pass rates were seen among high school students on ACT exams, according to the Arizona Department of Education.
